summary: Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann (1775–1839) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at Mainz (1787–1796) and Würzburg (1792–1796). He held posts at Lyceum Hosianum (1803), Hofbibliothek Aschaffenburg (1811), and as professor at the University of Bonn (1818).

Karl Lachmann (1793–1851) worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1809–1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812–1815), and held a post at the University of Berlin from around 1825 to 1851.

Karl Otfried Müller (1797–1840) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Breslau and Berlin, learning under Boeckh, Schleiermacher, and Wolf. He held posts at Magdalenaeum Wrocław (1818–1819) and the University of Göttingen from 1819.

Karl Popper (1902–1994) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Cambridge. His career included posts at the University of Canterbury (1937–1945), London School of Economics (1946), King's College London, and University of London (1949–1969).

Karl Rosenkranz (1805–1879) worked in philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Berlin under Hegel, and Halle. He held academic posts at the University of Halle (~1831–1833) before assuming a chair and rectorate at the University of Königsberg in 1833.

Karl Verner (1846–1896) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Aarhus Katedralskole, the University of Copenhagen, and under August Leskien. He served at Halle-Wittenberg's library (~1876–1883) and as docent in Slavic studies at Copenhagen (1882).

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck (born 1948) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Augsburg and Munich. His career includes posts at the University of Munich (1978–1988) and as professor at Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding (born 1953) is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD from the University of Bonn and his habilitation from the University of Hamburg. He worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1993) and the University of Hamburg (1999).
Karl-Heinz Gottmann (1919–2007) worked in Buddhist studies. He was the main student of Anagarika Govinda (~1952–1985) and succeeded him from 1982 to 1999.
Karma Lek Shé Drayang was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo (born 1944) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Tenzin Gyatso and at the University of Hawaiʻi. Her posts include the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and Numata Professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (2023).

Karma Phuntsho (born 1968) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Chagri, Sera, Ngagyur Nyingma Institute, and Oxford under Michael Aris, Richard Gombrich, and David Seyfort Ruegg. He held research posts at CNRS and the University of Cambridge.

Karma Sonam Palmo specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed her PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Thinley Rinpoche (born 1931) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as abbot at the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling, and founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling and Tekchen Lekshay Ling.

Karma Ura (born 1961) works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, Oxford, and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (1999–2008).

Karsé Kongtrul was a scholar who studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, the 13th Dalai Lama, and Khakyab Dorje. He also taught figures such as Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karuna Kusalasaya (1920–2009) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
Karunapati Tripathi was an Indologist who taught Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and President of the Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan.

Karunesh Shukla (born 1940) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under V. P. Upadhyaya. He held posts at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, including Reader (attested 1973) and Professor and Head of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages (attested 1991).

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz (born 1958) is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Central Asian studies. She studied at the University of Bonn (1978–1999) and held posts at the University of Bern as full professor (from 1999) and dean (2007–2010).
